catalog_quote: 2.1.2. Ударение – силовое, динамическое; падает на последний слог (в имени); вызывает редукцию безударного гласного (напр. жогъул 'лето' – жогъла 'летом'); в многосложном глаголе два ударения – в начале и в конце, ср. аш-не-беса 'работает'. Долгота гласного также может иметь фонологический характер: эхне 'говорит' – э:хне 'говорит без конца, долго'; унекса 'ест' – у:некса 'ест без конца, жадно'.

new_statements.quote: Удареніе не такъ сильно, какъ въ другихъ языкахъ и почти всегда ставится на послѣднемъ слогѣ слова. Впрочемъ, это правило имѣетъ исключенія; вотъ самыя главныя: 1) Слова, въ составъ которыхъ входятъ указательныя частицы ha, ḳa, те, ме, имѣютъ удареніе почти всегда на этихъ послѣднихъ [...] 2) На коренномъ слогѣ имѣютъ глаголы обыкновенно удареніе въ неопредѣленномъ и повелительномъ наклоненіяхъ и въ нѣкоторыхъ временахъ изъявительнаго накл. [...] 4) Удареніе не ставится никогда на нѣкоторыхъ словахъ и частицахъ, которыя соединяются такъ тѣсно со словомъ, имъ предшествующимъ, что ихъ нельзя разъединить въ письмѣ. (p. 3-4) [...] Примѣчаніе. Мы обозначаемъ слогъ, имѣющій удареніе, посредствомъ accent grave. (p. 5)
new_statements.translation: Stress is not as strong as in other languages and is almost always placed on the last syllable of the word. This rule, however, has exceptions; the main ones are: 1) Words containing the demonstrative particles ha, ḳa, te, me almost always carry the stress on these latter [...] 2) Verbs usually have the stress on the root syllable in the infinitive and imperative moods and in some tenses of the indicative [...] 4) Stress is never placed on certain words and particles which are joined so closely to the preceding word that they cannot be separated from it in writing. (pp. 3-4) [...] Note. We mark the stressed syllable with an accent grave. (p. 5)

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (StressTyp2 final stress = final stress): Dirr says stress is 'almost always' on the last syllable. He adds that stress is weak, that there is no vowel length, and a list of morphological exceptions (demonstrative particles, verb-root stress in infinitive/imperative, tense-marker stress, stressless clitics, strongly stressed negators), so the record is refined rather than contradicted.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is weak and falls on the final syllable of the word by default. Morphologically conditioned exceptions: (1) words built with the demonstrative particles ha, ḳa, te, me are stressed on those particles (hàšor, mètär, tèsahat); (2) verbs stress the root syllable in the infinitive, imperative and some indicative tenses when the element order is root + pronominal element + tense marker (c̣amc̣esun, c̣amc̣a, c̣amzuko); (3) when that order is changed the stress mostly moves to the tense marker (byğène, esàne, c̣amkàlzu), the causative particle -es- takes stress (akèstesun), and participles in -i / -al are stressed on the last syllable (c̣amc̣ì, ukàl); (4) pronominal clitic-infixes (zu, nu, ne..), the particle ṭe after pronouns, the interrogative a, and the particles al, kena, gena, a, no and the conjunction qan, and the suffix o, are never stressed; the prohibitive/negative particles te, nu(t), ma always take very strong stress and the following verb is nearly stressless. Also: no long/short vowel contrast (all vowels of medium duration, rather short); in questions the last syllable of the questioned word is lengthened.
new_statements.exceptions: Demonstrative-particle words stressed on the particle; verb root stress in infinitive/imperative and some indicative tenses; tense-marker stress when the element order changes; causative -es- stressed; participles in -i/-al stressed finally; enclitic pronominal infixes and particles (ṭe, a, al, kena, gena, a, no, qan, suffix o) never stressed; negative/prohibitive particles te, nu(t), ma strongly stressed with the following verb almost unstressed. Dirr's marking of stress uses an accent grave.
new_statements.identity_note: Dirr's grammar describes the Vartashen (Vartashen/Oğuz) variety of Udi: the preface (pp. X-XI, PDF page 9) says he intends to take up the Nidzh dialect later and thanks his informants Sogomoniants and Mnatsakaniants and his hosts for his stay in Vartashen. The stress statements therefore hold for Vartashen Udi as spoken c. 1903.

tone_statements.translation: SYLLABLE AND PROSODY. 1. Typical syllable structures ... 2. Pharyngealization spreads over the whole word when there are no uvulars or shibilants; in that case it is marked on the first vowel. ... 3. The accentual system has not been studied. Word stress is absent; the placement of the phrasal accent within the word has not been investigated. Syllabic tone may be present.

tone_statements.summary: Tentative only: no tone inventory; the author states there is no word stress in Nidzh Udi and that syllable-level tone is possible but uninvestigated; pharyngealization behaves as a word-domain prosody (maximum on the first vowel, or on a uvular/shibilant if present).

audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant (final): keep final as the default position but drop counts as exceptionless (the strict set). All three specialist sources hedge: Dzheiranishvili 2001 limits final stress to nouns ('в имени') and gives verbs two stresses; Talibov & Maisak 2005 p.181 say stress 'also occurs on the first syllable' (ттéсагьат, мéтаьр) and 'no clear rules governing stress have been identified'; Schulze 2001 §2.5 says the final syllable is stressed 'in many instances', with clitics unstressed and some particles inherently stressed. Also populate quote/cite/loc/grade from the domain quotation/the domain locator (currently empty) and add Talibov & Maisak 2005 p.181 and Schulze 2001 §2.5 as corroborating citations.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified on the scan we hold at printed p.454 §2.1.2 (image-only PDF; scanned + page scan). (2) Deciding source is a 2001 encyclopedic sketch; the held Talibov & Maisak 2005 sketch (Maisak is the leading current Udi fieldworker) and Schulze's 2001 online grammar §2.5, downloaded now from the the Internet Archive, independently confirm predominantly final dynamic stress, so the position coding is safe. (3) But every source qualifies the rule (initial stress in deictic-containing words, double stress in polysyllabic verbs, pre-clitic stress, 'no clear rules identified'), so 'fixed-strict' overstates the descriptions; 'fixed-dominant' final matches them. (4) The open-access Gippert & Dum-Tragut 2023 handbook (downloaded, 753 pp) has no modern-Udi stress rule. sources.citation: Schulze, Wolfgang. 2001. The Udi Language: A grammatical description with sample text (online grammar, LMU Munich), ch. 2 'Phonological system', §2.5 Stress. Internet Archive copy 2009-09-04 ofhttp://www.lrz-muenchen.de/~wschulze/udiphon.htm
sources.quote: 'Today, the stress pattern of Udi resembles that of Azeri (historically, Udi had its words stressed on the first or second syllable). In many instances, the final syllable is stressed. Yet, a considerable number of en- or endoclitics provoke the accentuation of the preceding syllable (cf. section 3.3.3 for personal agreement clitics). Some particles call for a clitic because of their inherent stress, e.g. q'a- (adh), gi- (cond), te- (neg), e.g. téne baksà, bürmišq'áq'un bi, campegízui.'
